variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE polished, coherent concept-design board for the COMPLETE BORDER WORLD PIRATE FIGHTER FAMILY from Freelancer (2003), redesigned around the actual original cabins. Three different ship classes designed together by the same shipyard, with an authentic early-2000s Freelancer industrial design language. This is a deliberate geometric redesign for future game modeling, not just repainting the reference.

REFERENCE ROLES IN EXACT INPUT ORDER:
1. Actual three native ships in deployed FLIGHT, equal scale: columns FIGHTER, ELITE, VHEAVY. Authority for each ship's identity, cabin placement, relative dimensions, layout and silhouette.
2. Close-ups of the ORIGINAL BW CABIN, shell and glazing. The native glazing geometry is identical across this family; use this close-up together with each full ship in reference 1. Immutable visual identity for ALL THREE, not a suggestion to draw a new cockpit.
3. Historical bw_elite sketch: inspiration ONLY for sharp nose, stepped volumes, high vertical composition and angular wing planes. Its long greenhouse canopy is NOT permitted.
4. Native VHEAVY motion: first column is deployed flight; last is stowed. Use deployed state on every final view. The wings and outer side sections translate sideways, not rotate.
5. Native cargo lid: two opening dorsal leaves behind the cabin. Keep this functional roof zone unobstructed.

CRITICAL IMMUTABLE CABINS:
Reproduce each original small low faceted cockpit from references 1 and 2 in every view. Same blue-grey window shape, same window arrangement, original thick metal surrounds, same sloped roof, original complete cabin silhouette, size and position. Preserve the front clipped polygonal pane and the slanted broad side pane with its native thick framing. This is the user's most important requirement. No new canopy design, elongated greenhouse, spherical glass, bubble, glowing slit, new windshield divisions, helmet or face. The new hull is designed around that exact existing cabin. Keep cabin size consistent between the three ships.

LAYOUT:
One high-resolution PORTRAIT board, aspect ratio about 2:3, warm ivory paper, restrained technical lettering. Three generously spaced HORIZONTAL ROWS:
TOP = FIGHTER; MIDDLE = ELITE; BOTTOM = VHEAVY.
Each row contains one LARGE front three-quarter view at left, and two smaller clearly separated orthographic studies at right: SIDE above TOP. All three main perspectives use the same camera and comparable physical scale. Exactly three ship designs, each shown in these three consistent views. No aircraft overlaps another, nothing cropped. Side and top views must match their main perspective geometrically. Thin row separators. Keep labels short. No ornamental diagram arrows, no unrelated sketches, no scenery.

CLASS ARCHITECTURE:
FIGHTER: low horizontal single-level body, long tapered pointed nose ahead of the cabin, one compact rear-facing centerline engine, one broad pair of angular wings. NO hanging lower engine or vertical keel.
ELITE: shares the recognizable upper hull and nose grammar, adds a tall solid faceted central keel below it, a second smaller rear-facing engine in a low centerline gondola, and upper plus lower wing pairs. Retain broad open space to each side of the central keel. No outer enclosing side loops.
VHEAVY: same length and height as ELITE, only slightly wider, also exactly two rear-facing engines stacked vertically, central keel and lower gondola. Its distinctive TWO LARGE OPEN SIDE WINDOWS must remain readable in the main view: one on each side of the central keel, bounded by upper wing and lower outboard sections. Reinterpret their perimeter as integrated flattened faceted hull/wing surfaces with meaningful thickness, not thin rods, a cage, a tubular hoop or latticework. Do not fill these large openings with armor. Draw separate telescoping interfaces where moving upper/outboard units approach lower wings; do not weld the movable exterior perimeter to the fixed gondola. Do not turn this fighter into a freighter or inflate it.

MECHANICAL AND ARTISTIC LANGUAGE:
The family must share the same few characteristic angular shoulder cuts, recessed trapezoidal fields, short broad inset grilles, engine shroud sections and substantial closed slider housings. Clear joined forms, sharp corners, varied plane depths and controlled medium-scale detail; enough richness to exceed the original geometry, but spacious readable hull surfaces remain. Visible mechanical interest should come from shaped recesses, panel seating and real motion interfaces. Preserve dorsal twin baydoor leaves behind each cabin; show their clear split and lateral hinges with free swing space above. Wings translate inward when stowed; do not invent rotary folding hinges. Show flight with wings extended.
Native pirate material character: worn warm pale grey / tan metal, restrained faded rusty-orange donor sections, charcoal recessed machinery and blue-grey glass. Secondary repair seams and asymmetrically replaced panels should support the designed form. Engine interiors dark, no huge glowing plumes. Neutral studio illumination, carefully shaded painterly production concept art, precise silhouettes. Medium detail, not noisy microdetail.

EXCLUDE:
New cockpit shapes, Rheinland drums/discs, generic modern jet canopies, demons/skulls/teeth/horns, decorative pirate flags, literal airboat fans, external pipes/hoses/cables, skeletal frameworks, thin braces, rivet fields, dense greeble, turrets or long gun barrels added to fake complexity. No large spheres, no disconnected boxes, no generic rounded sci-fi pods. No new parked/stowed drawings on the final board.

SPECIFIC DESIGN DIRECTION B01 — SWEPT FACETED CUTS:
Title verbatim: "BW PIRATE — B01". Row labels verbatim: "FIGHTER", "ELITE", "VHEAVY"; small view labels "SIDE" and "TOP".
Make this a lean, sharp, convincingly redesigned BW family. Develop a long stepped spear-shaped forebody AROUND the native cabin; give shoulder planes a distinctive diagonal recessed cut that repeats at each wing root and on the heavy central keel. Wings have a broad sharp clipped tip, a modest angular trailing-edge notch and a single deep trapezoidal root pocket. Connect the main engine shroud to the hull through continuous faceted transitions. ELITE's keel is a tapered blade with one deep elongated recess and a strong flared seat at the lower engine. VHEAVY's outboard window margins are swept, flat, multi-plane wing sections with broad chamfer-shaped profile transitions and local cutouts, light enough to keep the two big windows open. NO narrow skeletal bars. One pale donor patch and a restrained orange band vary between the three classes. This is a change of primary planes, wing roots and joining volumes, not a surface-decoration pass. Cabin remains exact.

Develop a distinctly different, workmanlike pirate family with compact stepped shoulders and deep angular saddle-shaped wing-root sockets. Retain the original long sharp nose and EXACT native low cabin, but redesign the forebody with a broken diagonal side contour and two broad recessed fields separated by a structural step. Wings terminate in sharpened asymmetric clipped polygon shapes, with a deep squared notch at the trailing inner corner. Main engine shell is a compact faceted enclosure with a broad inset side grille integrated into the rear hull. ELITE's central keel has an offset angular side pocket and a two-step saddle around the lower engine, while retaining its tall thin lateral profile. VHEAVY has broader short shoulder surfaces and stepped angular outboard side-window margins, like solid armor-wing sections around two generously open trapezoidal windows; keep thickness localized at mounts and leave the long stretches visually light. No outer frame added to ELITE. Shared heavy rectangular/trapezoidal mechanical seats, deep low-count recesses and visibly patched pale metal with restrained orange replacement sections. All three must look like the same family and differ substantially from B01's continuous swept cuts. Neither extra overall bulk nor higher microdetail is the solution. Cabin remains exact.
